paper_title: Detecting Entanglement by State Preparation and Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim; Anindita Bera; Dariusz Chruściński; Joonwoo Bae
statement: computes the singlet fidelity [49], meaning that σ ⊗ N is not PPT, also signifying that either σ or N should be non-PPT. It is also clear that if both σ and N are PPT, then a state σ ⊗ N remains PPT under LOCC. Note that distillable entangled states must be non-PPT although the converse remains open; it has been a long-standing open question whether non-PPT states are distillable [45, 51]. Stated equivalently, a PPT entangled state can activate a non-PPT state, but not another PPT state. Hence, a network state N23 to detect a PPT entangled state ρ1 should be non-PPT. We thus conclude that multipartite non-PPT entangled states can construct non-decomposable EWs, which are highly non-trivial. Note that non-PPT states can construct both decomposable and nondecomposable EWs, as shown in the example of reduction EWs, see Eq. (24).
